2027-03-16.title: Sixth Tuesday of the Great Fast
2027-03-16.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The Lord knows how to rescue the godly
2027-03-16.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-03-16.verse: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it! How often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!
theo: The Second Letter of Peter was written to Christians troubled by teachers who mocked God's judgement and lived as they pleased. Peter answers with three examples from the Scriptures: the angels who sinned, the world of Noah's flood, and the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. In each case God did not let evil have the last word. But in each case he also saved someone. He “saved Noah, a herald of righteousness, with seven others”, and “he rescued Lot, a righteous man greatly distressed by the licentiousness of the lawless (for that righteous man, living among them day after day, was tormented in his righteous soul by their lawless deeds that he saw and heard)”. Peter's conclusion is full of comfort: “the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial.” Lot was no great hero; Genesis tells us that he lingered, and the angels had to take him by the hand. Yet he had not grown used to the evil around him; it tormented his soul. That is a sign of life. Many of us live, study or work among habits that slowly dull the conscience. The Great Fast asks: am I still distressed by what is wrong, or have I made my peace with it? The Lord who took Lot by the hand can lead us out too.

In the Gospel some Pharisees come to warn Jesus: “Get away from here, for Herod wants to kill you.” Not every Pharisee was his enemy; some here seem to want to protect him. Jesus will not run. “Go and tell that fox for me, ‘Listen, I am casting out demons and performing cures today and tomorrow, and on the third day I finish my work.’” Herod is a fox, cunning but small; Jesus' path is set by the Father, and it leads to Jerusalem and to the third day. Then his voice changes, and he speaks not in anger but in grief: “Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it! How often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!” This is the voice of a mother, not a judge. The image is tender and costly: a hen spreads her wings over her chicks when danger comes, and takes the fire or the hawk on herself. That is what Jesus will do on the Cross. His lament is not a condemnation of the Jewish people, whom God has never ceased to love; it is the grief of love over every human heart that refuses to be gathered, and so it is addressed to us. Next Sunday we will cry “Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord”; today we ask whether we are willing to be gathered under his wings.
outline: Ask: am I still troubled by what is wrong around me?
Point 1 · The Lord knows how to rescue
Noah, Lot, and the godly in every age.
Jesus does not turn from his road.
Point 3 · As a hen gathers her brood
The grief of love, and our answer.
“How often have I desired to gather your children together.”
live: Name one habit around you that no longer troubles you, and ask the Lord to make you sensitive again.
Spend ten quiet minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week, simply letting yourself be gathered.
2027-03-16.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you set your face toward Jerusalem and did not turn back. As a hen gathers her brood under her wings, you long to gather us. Keep our consciences awake among the evils of our time, take us by the hand when we linger, and make us willing to be gathered under your wings. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Lord who longed to gather Jerusalem's children gathers us around one altar, and gives us the Body that was given up for us, as a mother bird shields her young with her own body.

quick: The Lord knows how to rescue the godly, as he rescued Noah and Lot.
Jesus will not flee Herod; his road leads to Jerusalem and the third day.
He longs to gather us like a hen gathering her brood.
2027-03-16.action: Spend ten quiet minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week.
2027-03-16.question: Am I willing to be gathered, or do I keep running from his wings?

family.explain: Jesus said he was like a mother hen. When a hawk comes, the hen calls her chicks and spreads her wings over them, so that they are safe. Jesus wants to keep us close and safe like that. But the chicks have to come when she calls!
family.intention: We pray for children who are lost or alone, that someone may gather them in.
family.ask: Ask: “When Jesus calls us this week, how can we run to him?”

illus: After a fire in a farmyard in Kuttanad, the owner walked through the ashes and found a hen lying dead, burnt black. When he nudged her with his stick, three chicks ran out from under her wings, alive. She had stayed over them while the fire passed. The old man who told this story in his parish every Lent always ended the same way: “That is what he meant. He stayed over us while the fire passed.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you long to gather us under your wings. Here we are; gather us now. Amen.
share: The Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial (2 Peter 2:9). Where do I need to be rescued?
Go and tell that fox (Luke 13:32). What threatens to turn me from the road God has set for me?
How often have I desired to gather your children together (Luke 13:34). Where have I been unwilling?
pm.resp: Lord, gather us under your wings.
interc: For the Church, that she may gather all peoples with the love of Christ.
For Christians who live among pressures that dull the conscience.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in faithfulness to his covenant.
For children who are lost, unprotected or alone.
For our group, that we may not resist the Lord's call.
pm.close: Father, your Son longed to gather your children as a hen gathers her brood. Make us willing to be gathered, and rescue us in every trial. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Peter reminds his readers that God saved Noah and rescued Lot, a righteous man tormented by the lawless deeds he saw and heard every day. Then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial (2 Peter 2:9).
Lot was troubled by the evil around him; he had not grown used to it. Let us ask whether our conscience is still awake, or whether we have quietly made peace with what is wrong.

In the Gospel Jesus is warned that Herod wants to kill him. He will not run: he must go on to Jerusalem. And he weeps over the city: how often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings (Luke 13:34).
This is the grief of love, and it is spoken to every heart that refuses to be gathered, including ours. On the Cross he spread his arms like wings over us. This week, let us come under them. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said he is like a mother hen who keeps her chicks safe under her wings. When you are afraid, run to Jesus in prayer, and he will hold you close.

intro: Theme: “How often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!”
God who rescues the righteous, and the Lord who will not turn from Jerusalem, grieving over every heart that refuses to be gathered.

then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment until the day of judgment
points.apply: Name one habit around you that no longer troubles you, and ask God to awaken your conscience.

points.h: I must be on my way
sub: Today, tomorrow and the third day.
q: The Lord God helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame;
Yet today, tomorrow, and the next day I must be on my way, because it is impossible for a prophet to be killed outside of Jerusalem.
points.apply: Do not let fear of others' opinion turn you from one good thing you know you must do this week.

sub: The hen that shields her young.
q: he will cover you with his pinions, and under his wings you will find refuge; his faithfulness is a shield and buckler.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it! How often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!
points.apply: Spend ten quiet minutes before the Blessed Sacrament, letting the Lord gather you.

concl: God rescues the godly, and his Son goes on to Jerusalem to spread his arms over us on the Cross.
His lament is the grief of love; our answer is to be willing to be gathered.
2027-03-16.resolve: Keep your conscience awake this week, and come under his wings in silent prayer.
